segments.t: Inspired by German's remark, Viktor approaches the owner of Arcobaleno in the dining room and tries to get himself fired on the spot—with unexpected results. Listen in Russian first.
Позвольте засвидетельствовать лично почтение вам.
Спасибо.
А давайте накатим, ну, для сближения.
Ой, что-то я рановато стал.
Извините, я вас вытру сейчас.
Вы с ума сошли!
Вот потрясающий вкус, особенно филейной части.
А что случилось?
Что вы делаете здесь, Виктор Петрович?
Зря я послушал вас, Елена Павловна.
И согласился взять этого человека.
Просто хотел поближе познакомиться.
Let's look closely at each Russian line in this scene.
Позвольте засвидетельствовать лично почтение вам.

'Allow me to personally pay my respects to you.' Telling Elena to allow him to personally pay his respects to Elena is how Barinov lays out the situation for Elena. Notice how he sticks to the formal "you", keeping a professional line between them.
Спасибо.
'Thank you.' Realizing that Barinov should thank Barinov changes how the guest handles the situation.
А давайте накатим, ну, для сближения.

'Let's have a drink together, just to bond.' Proposing that they have a drink together just to bond moves the conversation forward without extra drama. Starting with "davay" is the everyday Russian way to say "come on, let us do this".
Ой, что-то я рановато стал.
'Oops, I started pouring a little too early.' Saying that someone he started pouring a little too early is how Barinov sets the tone with Elena.
Извините, я вас вытру сейчас.
'Excuse me, I will wipe that off for you right now.' Once he will wipe that off for Elena right now, Barinov can finally tell Elena what he means.
Вы с ума сошли!

'Have you lost your mind!' The guest insists that have Barinov lost Barinov's mind, leaving Barinov no room to argue. Even in the middle of the drama, he keeps the polite plural "you" that workplace Russian expects.
Вот потрясающий вкус, особенно филейной части.
'What an amazing flavor, especially the fillet part.' With the work and wine in play, Barinov keeps this short reply brisk and direct.
А что случилось?
'What happened here?' With the conversation and wine hanging in the air, Elena puts Barinov on the spot.
Что вы делаете здесь, Виктор Петрович?

'What are you doing out here, Viktor Petrovich?' By asking what Barinov doing out here Viktor Petrovich is, Elena presses Barinov for a straight answer. Notice how she sticks to the formal "you", keeping a professional line between them.
Зря я послушал вас, Елена Павловна.

'It was a mistake for me to listen to you, Elena Pavlovna.' The guest reminds Barinov that it was a mistake for him to listen to Barinov Elena Pavlovna before the moment passes. Even in the middle of the drama, he keeps the polite plural "you" that workplace Russian expects.
И согласился взять этого человека.
'And agree to hire this man.' Admitting that Barinov should agree to hire this man shows the guest being honest for a change.
Просто хотел поближе познакомиться.

'I simply wanted to get better acquainted.' Explaining that he simply wanted to get better acquainted lays the cards on the table for Elena. With all the phrases clear, listen to the full Russian dialogue again.

И согласился взять этого человека.
Просто хотел поближе познакомиться.
That covers Viktor's failed attempt to get fired by offending the owner of Arcobaleno. Notice how formal greetings contrast with colloquial drinking slang. Until next time!
Всего хорошего!
